items.description: Running the stock_records Alembic migration downgrade followed immediately by upgrade completes without error on the real branch database

After the stock_records Alembic migration upgrade completes, a row inserted with a per-run-unique key is persisted with its original column values when read back from the real branch database, confirming the migration created the table with the correct structure
The boundary layer (app/routes/) contains no import of a SQLAlchemy session object
The service layer (app/services/) contains no import of any SQLAlchemy ORM symbol (model class or session)
The boundary layer (app/routes/) contains no import of any SQLAlchemy ORM model class
The application resolves its database connection exclusively from the DATABASE_URL environment variable with no hardcoded connection string present in source
The integration test suite connects via a DATABASE_URL that resolves to a real Postgres driver and not an in-memory or mocked database engine
Filing stock through the API with a per-run-unique SKU, a location, a quantity, and an inventory_code persists a record that is subsequently retrievable from the database with those exact values
A boundary validation error response for a bad filing request includes the name of the specific field that failed validation rather than a generic error message
The service layer raises a rejection error when a filed quantity is negative, before the write reaches the database
Attempting to insert a stock record with a null sku value is rejected by the NOT NULL constraint on the stock_records table against the real branch database
Attempting to insert a stock record with a null location value is rejected by the NOT NULL constraint on the stock_records table against the real branch database
Attempting to insert a stock record with a null inventory_code value is rejected by the NOT NULL constraint on the stock_records table against the real branch database
Attempting to insert a stock record with a null quantity value is rejected by the NOT NULL constraint on the stock_records table against the real branch database
Attempting to insert a stock record with a negative integer quantity is rejected by the ck_stock_records_quantity_non_negative CHECK constraint at the real branch database
Retrieving a previously filed stock record through the API returns the exact quantity and inventory_code as originally filed
Every stock endpoint in the boundary layer (app/routes/) returns a JSON-encoded response body and invokes no server-side HTML template renderer
Filing stock twice for the same per-run-unique SKU and location pair through the API updates the existing record in place with no duplicate row stored and no error surfaced to the caller
Filing a second stock record for an existing (sku, location) pair produces exactly one row in stock_records rather than inserting a duplicate, verified against the real branch database
Concurrent writes targeting the same (sku, location) pair result in exactly one row in stock_records owing to the single-transaction upsert, verified against the real branch database
An in-place upsert on an existing (sku, location) row leaves the created_at timestamp unchanged from its value at original filing time
